findings.what: The activity chunk mapping drops `attempt`, so every Attempt cell on the activity page shows a dash, and the page says a dash means the log has no value. The log has one.
findings.why: Every activity.jsonl line carries attempt (e.g. docs/trace/ui/U0b/activity.jsonl:1, and the complete fixture's lines 1-5 hold attempt 1). The signed-off contract reads trace/<plan>/<node>/activity.json[].attempt (docs/ui/derived/U0b/activity/screen.json:17,26). Activity.tsx:46 renders `row.record.attempt ?? GAP`, and Activity.tsx:107 tells the reader 'A dash means the log holds none for that column'. Showing an absence the trail contradicts is a claim that isn't in the trail (ui-requirements HONEST-1; principle 'show the receipt, not the claim'). The fix belongs in the compiler (carry attempt into the chunk), not in the screen.

findings.what: The activity row read-back checks Line, Agent, Tool, command, Commit and TDD but skips Attempt. The compiler's chunk test maps only agent/tool/file/command. Neither sees R1.
findings.why: Success tests must read the resource back in full through the shared assertion (reviewer check 3; requirements-trace 'Stub-proof success rows'). A partial read-back let a missing column pass 64/64 at loop.jsonl:71. tests/web/unit/compiler/data-1.test.ts:103 likewise omits attempt (and ts) from the chunk shape. No HONEST-1-tagged test asserts the activity values against the fixture trail. A red test should assert Attempt = 1 on rows 1-5 of the complete fixture, plus a chunk-shape assertion that includes attempt.

findings.what: Only the commit subject goes through the denylist scan. Emitted trailer values (Rule, Agent, Plan, Node, TDD, Fixes-Finding) and compiledAt.ref reach trace.json unscanned.
findings.why: DATA-5: 'The compiler fails the build if its output matches the privacy denylist'. The data-5 unit test header claims the scan covers 'every value it emits'. That is not so: index.ts:112-124 emits commits[].agent/plan/node/rule/tdd/fixesFinding from commit bodies, and :206 emits ref, with no scan(). Nothing else guards these values: .githooks/pre-commit scans staged files only, and commit-msg checks the Rule trailer only for being non-empty, so its free text is unguarded. The exposure is narrow (Agent, TDD and Fixes-Finding are pattern-checked by commit-msg), but the rule's guarantee isn't met and no test plants a denylisted trailer. Fix direction: scan the serialised output, or every emitted git-derived value, and add a red test with a denylisted Rule trailer.

findings.what: trailersOf uses Object.fromEntries, so a repeated trailer key keeps only its last value. Commits with several Fixes-Finding lines lose all but the last in trace.json.
findings.why: This trail repeats Fixes-Finding lines: 380ef5f has A1/I1 and A1/I2, and 99e9d93 has A2/I1, A2/I3 and A2/I4 (packet/trailers.txt). fixesFinding() at index.ts expects a comma list, but the trail writes one line per finding, so the compiled commits[].fixesFinding misstates the trail. No U0b screen reads it yet, but LOOP-2 (the retry ladder) will, and no test covers repeated trailers. That is why this is P2 and not P1.

findings.what: The compiler fills events, verdicts and rules[].status/feature/red/green with parsing logic that no U0b test drives and no U0b screen reads.
findings.why: The loop.jsonl event parse (:154-163), the verdict envelope and round parse (:164-179) and the rule status derivation (:189-200) have no red test in tests/web/unit/compiler (the DATA-1 tests check only the rule ids and the commit fields). The trace-data schema needs the lists to exist, but filling them with untested logic is code not driven by a red commit (web-testing: green follows red), and it is speculative for this node (code-quality slop list). Either test it here or emit empty lists until U1/U3 drive it.
